en: n. the act of getting something, especially by buying it; something that you have bought or obtained; the process of learning a skill; the buying of one company by another
ex: The company announced the acquisition of a small software firm.
公司宣布收購一家小型軟體公司。

en: n. something that encourages someone to do something; a reward or bonus that makes people work harder; a. encouraging someone to do something
ex: The company offers a bonus as an incentive to work harder.
公司提供獎金以激勵員工更努力工作。

en: n. a person who sells things, especially on the street; a company that sells goods; a machine that sells things such as drinks and snacks
ex: A street vendor was selling fried rice cakes.
一位街頭小販正在賣炸年糕。

en: vt. to change something slightly to improve it; to make something less extreme; to change the meaning of a word or phrase; vi. to be changed
ex: The company decided to modify its product design.
公司決定修改產品設計。

en: n. an idea or understanding of something; the start of a pregnancy; the beginning of an idea or project; the ability to form ideas
ex: She has no conception of how difficult the job is.
她完全不知道這工作有多困難。

en: vt. to cause something to turn upside down; to officially decide that a previous decision is wrong; to defeat or remove someone from power; vi. to turn over; n. a surprising defeat of a favored person or team
ex: The court overturned the earlier ruling.
法院推翻了先前的判決。

en: n. an urgent and emotional request; a formal statement a person makes in court, such as guilty or not guilty; an excuse; (formal) a legal case
ex: He made a plea for help to his neighbors.
他向鄰居求助。

en: n. the way in which something is arranged or presented; the size and shape of a book or magazine; the way in which data is stored on a computer disk; vt. to prepare a disk so that data can be stored on it; to arrange something in a particular way
ex: The format of the exam has changed this year.
今年考試的格式有所改變。

en: n. a person who answers questions in a survey; a person who has been accused of something in a court case; a person who replies; a. giving a response
ex: More than half of the respondents said they liked the new design.
超過半數的受訪者表示喜歡新設計。
ph: a respondent in a divorce case

en: n. a shape made by a line that curves back on itself; a piece of rope or wire shaped like a circle; a part of a computer program that is repeated until a condition is met; vt. to form something into a loop; vi. to move in a circle
ex: Tie a loop at the end of the rope.
在繩子的尾端打一個圈。

en: n. the large size or quantity of something; the main part of something; a large amount; vt. to look large or important; vi. to grow larger
ex: Most of the cargo is in bulk, like grain and coal.
大部分貨物是散裝的，像穀物和煤炭。

en: n. something that is given or offered to someone; a gift offered to God; a product or service that a company offers; the act of offering something for sale
ex: The restaurant has a wide range of lunch offerings.
這家餐廳提供多種午餐選擇。

en: n. the act of finding out what illness a person has by examining them; a decision about what is wrong with someone or something; the process of identifying the cause of a problem
ex: The doctor made a quick diagnosis of the patient's illness.
醫生很快診斷出病人的病因。

en: vt. to cause a strong reaction, especially anger; to make someone angry; to cause something to happen; to try to make someone argue or fight
ex: His rude comment provoked an angry response.
他的粗魯言論引來憤怒的回應。

en: a. relating to a city or town; relating to the duties of citizens; relating to the community
ex: It is our civic duty to vote in elections.
投票是我們的公民義務。

en: vt. to allow yourself or someone else to have what they want; to spoil someone by being too kind or generous; vi. to allow yourself to enjoy something you like
ex: She indulged herself with a piece of chocolate cake.
她放縱自己吃了一塊巧克力蛋糕。

en: n. energy that comes from a source in the form of rays or waves; a dangerous form of energy produced by nuclear reactions; the sending out of heat or light
ex: Too much radiation can be harmful to the human body.
過量輻射對人體有害。

en: n. a plant whose leaves or seeds are used to flavor food or as medicine; a small plant with leaves used in cooking; a plant used to treat illness
ex: She grows herbs like basil and mint in her garden.
她在花園裡種了羅勒和薄荷等香草。

en: vi. to bring food up from your stomach through your mouth; vt. to bring something up from the stomach; n. food that has been brought up from the stomach
ex: The child vomited after eating too much candy.
孩子吃太多糖果後吐了。

en: a. more than enough; large in size or amount; enough for what is needed
ex: There is ample room for everyone in the hall.
大廳裡有足夠的空間容納所有人。

en: vt. to use something fully; to treat someone unfairly in order to get a benefit; to develop something to get a benefit; n. a brave or exciting act
ex: Some companies exploit cheap labor in other countries.
有些公司剝削其他國家的廉價勞工。

en: n. an area of knowledge or activity; the land owned or controlled by a ruler or government; a set of internet addresses; the area of a particular activity
ex: This topic is outside my domain of expertise.
這個主題不在我的專業領域內。

en: vt. to cause a feeling or reaction in someone; to wake someone from sleep; to encourage someone to take action; vi. to wake up
ex: The strange noise aroused his curiosity.
那奇怪的聲響引起了他的好奇心。

en: n. a drug or other substance used to treat a disease or condition; the treatment of an illness with drugs; medicine taken by a patient
ex: The patient is taking medication for high blood pressure.
病人正在服用治療高血壓的藥物。

en: a. coming before the main part of something; happening before a more important event; n. something that comes before the main event; a first round in a sports competition
ex: The preliminary results show that the plan is working.
初步結果顯示這項計畫奏效了。

en: vt. to make something more modern by adding the latest information; to give someone the latest information; vi. to install the newest version; n. a new version of something; the latest information about something
ex: Please update the software to the latest version.
請把軟體更新到最新版本。

en: vt. to move soldiers or equipment into position; to use something effectively; to spread something out in an organized way; vi. to take up a position
ex: The army deployed troops along the border.
軍隊沿著邊境部署了部隊。

en: a. having the necessary ability or skills to do something well; good enough but not excellent; having legal power to do something
ex: She is a competent manager who handles problems well.
她是個稱職的經理，處理問題很有一套。

en: n. a very stupid person; (informal) someone who does something very foolish; (offensive) a person with very low intelligence
ex: I felt like an idiot when I forgot her name.
我忘了她的名字，覺得自己像個白痴。

en: n. a set of clothes worn together, especially for a particular occasion; a set of equipment or tools; (informal) a business or organization; vt. to provide someone with clothes or equipment
ex: She wore a stylish outfit to the party.
她穿了一套時尚的服裝去參加派對。

en: a. that must be done because of a rule or law; forced; required by law or rules; (of a subject at school) that every student must study
ex: Wearing seat belts is compulsory in most countries.
在大多數國家，繫安全帶是強制性的。

en: vt. to raise your shoulders slightly to show that you do not know or care about something; to dismiss something as unimportant; n. a movement of the shoulders to show that you do not care; v. to say something in a casual way
ex: He shrugged and said he didn't know the answer.
他聳聳肩說他不知道答案。

en: vt. to formally suggest someone for a job or a prize; to officially choose someone for a position; to choose a date or a name for something
ex: She was nominated for the Best Actress award.
她被提名角逐最佳女主角獎。

en: n. a flat thin square or rectangular piece of ceramic or stone used for covering floors, walls and roofs; a flat piece of material used for covering a surface; vt. to cover something with tiles
ex: They replaced the old tiles in the bathroom.
他們換掉了浴室裡的舊磁磚。

en: n. an attempt by a group of people to change the government by force; a refusal to obey rules or authority; an attempt to fight against someone in authority
ex: The army put down the rebellion within a week.
軍隊在一週內平定了叛亂。

en: n. the act of traveling around a place to learn about it; careful study of something; the act of examining something carefully; the search for new places
ex: Space exploration has taught us a lot about the universe.
太空探索讓我們對宇宙有了許多認識。

en: n. a sudden strong wish to do something without thinking about the results; a sudden push or force; a signal sent along a nerve; vt. to push something forward
ex: She bought the dress on impulse.
她一時衝動買了那件洋裝。

en: adv. above your head; high above; a. located above the ground; located above head level; n. the regular costs of running a business, such as rent and electricity
ex: Planes were flying overhead as we watched.
我們觀看時飛機正從頭頂飛過。

en: a. the total amount before anything is taken away; very offensive or rude; very unpleasant; n. a unit of twelve dozen; the total amount of something; vt. to earn a total amount of money before tax
ex: His gross income is fifty thousand dollars a year.
他的年總收入是五萬元。

en: n. the right of a country to rule itself; supreme authority over a territory; the power or right to rule; a self-governing state
ex: The island gained sovereignty after a long struggle.
這座島嶼經過長期奮鬥後取得主權。
